mcpTools.description: Reply to an ask by id and set its status (answered by default; decided or wontfix). The asker's next `inbox` shows it. Commits and pushes.
mcpTools.name: answer

mcpTools.description: Send a question to a role (backend, architect…) or a project in the team-brain; the member who holds it sees it in their `inbox`. Commits and pushes `asks/<id>.md`. A `to` nobody holds is refused with the roles and projects that exist.
mcpTools.name: ask

mcpTools.description: Append an explicit note to the vault; returns the path. In a repo connected to a team-brain this writes there automatically (one-file-per-note, auto commit+push).
mcpTools.name: capture

mcpTools.description: Assemble notes + team-brain git history since <since> as raw material for the agent to summarize.
mcpTools.name: catch_me_up

mcpTools.description: The API contracts the team's repos publish to the team-brain. With `project`: what it serves (method, path, operation id, response schema), calls and emits — narrow with `path`. With `calls`: which projects call an endpoint ("/items", "GET /items/{id}") and which serve it. With neither: the projects that have published one. Pulls first; every list is a floor.
mcpTools.name: contract

mcpTools.description: The code graph. In a repo, from its Cortex index: stats · node (file) · neighbors (file, depth 1-3) · cluster (cluster or file) · hubs · bridges · path (from, to, directed) · callers / callees (symbol) · defines (file), the last three when the parser add-on built symbols. On a team, from the team-brain: story (key: the code an epic or story touched, its clusters, contracts, untested files, hubs and open asks) · stories-for (file or cluster, with project) · risk (open stories touching untested or hub code). Refuses a missing or stale index or story links and names the command that rebuilds them. Lists are capped; every count is a floor.
mcpTools.name: graph

mcpTools.description: Open asks addressed to your roles or projects, and the answers to asks you sent. Pulls the team-brain first. Call it at the start of a task. `me.job` is your job in the team (developer when none is recorded).
mcpTools.name: inbox

mcpTools.description: List projects registered in the brain; in a repo joined to a team-brain, also the team's project files with their repo and links.
mcpTools.name: list_projects

mcpTools.description: Lexical search over the indexed markdown; returns ranked snippets with file paths.
mcpTools.name: recall

mcpTools.description: Read back recent days of this repo's committed memory, newest first.
mcpTools.name: recall_memory

mcpTools.description: Append a durable note to this repo's committed .cortex/memory/, in the author's own file for the day (<date>/<author>.md). Refuses anything carrying a credential — memory ships with the code. A `notice` in the result means the note went to the shared <date>.md instead: tell the user what it says.
mcpTools.name: remember

rituals.does: vault health: find + fix orphans, dead links, misplaced files, privacy leaks; `score` for the read-only four-layer score, `graph` to rebuild the navigator

rituals.does: interview in rounds until the design tree has no unresolved branch
rituals.name: challenge-plan

rituals.does: who depends on these files, and which of it no test covers; `--against` — where it collides with another session's change set; `--size` — one agent or a team, recommended
rituals.name: change-impact

rituals.does: the prompt gate — scores a vague prompt and sharpens it before work starts
rituals.name: clarify-request

rituals.does: install the Cortex Core plugin bundle, and register `mcp/server.js` at user scope for recall/capture
rituals.name: connect-mcp

rituals.does: create + seed the shared team-brain repo
rituals.name: create-team

rituals.does: open today's note; surface priorities + due items
rituals.name: daily-plan

rituals.does: build a red-capable loop first, ranked against the repo’s own invariants

rituals.does: sharpen that repo's glossary — write its `CONTEXT.md` + ADRs

rituals.does: compact this conversation to the OS temp dir for the next agent

rituals.does: clone the team-brain; drop `.cortex/connector.json`

rituals.does: judge it against the repo's docs, one PR at a time, merge in an order that strands nothing

rituals.does: move off the retired `.ai-os/` engine
rituals.name: migrate-legacy-engine

rituals.does: interview the user; fill `context/`, `home.md`, `connections.md`

rituals.does: one-line drop to `inbox/` or today's daily note

rituals.does: register personal repos into `projects/` — metadata only

rituals.does: render the index as one offline HTML page — overview, map, structure, files, areas, gaps

rituals.does: resolve a stuck merge/rebase by intent, hunk by hunk. Never `--abort`

rituals.does: committed · uncommitted · diverged, then what is left — before touching anything; where the repo is in the setup sequence, and the one command to run now

rituals.does: Notice→Decide→Build interview; ship one artifact

rituals.does: judge a change against the repo's own docs, and spot the ones it made wrong
rituals.name: review-change

rituals.does: show or set which world this install serves — home · work · lab

rituals.does: the single install: index, report, and stamp the whole SDLC loop in one pass, after one confirmation. A report-only path indexes and reports and writes nothing else
rituals.name: setup-repo

rituals.does: each epic traced to the code its stories touched, what waits on an open ask, where the risk is. Never estimates
rituals.name: story-map

rituals.does: propose + write skills that fit the detected stack

rituals.does: add summaries/roles/tags on top of the index. Costs tokens; optional

rituals.name: trim-agent-docs

rituals.does: make the Cortex this session runs the one you edited
rituals.name: update-plugin

rituals.does: empty `inbox/`, update `projects/`, restamp `current-focus`

rituals.does: brain notes + team-brain git history → what changed & why
rituals.name: whats-changed

rituals.does: the authoring discipline behind every file Cortex writes, and the steps that create and wire a new `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`
rituals.name: write-agent-docs
rituals.when: writing any agent-facing doc, or a new skill

rituals.does: write scoped `AGENTS.md` leaves + wire the root routing table
